findings.sourceEvidence: No Loan Party will, nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, create, incur, assume or permit to exist any Lien on any property or asset now owned or hereafter acquired by it...
findings.verifierReasoning: The source prohibition is not limited to acts by Loan Parties themselves - it also bars Loan Parties from 'permitting' any Restricted Subsidiary to create a Lien, meaning the substantive restriction reaches all Restricted Subsidiaries (including those that are not Loan Parties), not merely Loan Parties. This is confirmed by several of the exceptions themselves, which are explicitly framed around Restricted Subsidiary property/conduct independent of Loan Party status (e.g. (c) 'any property or asset of any Borrower or any Restricted Subsidiary', (d) 'any Loan Party or any Restricted Subsidiary', (g) 'a Restricted Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party'). By listing entityScope as only ["LOAN_PARTY"], the proposed IR understates the scope of the restriction and could lead a reviewer to conclude that a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary is free to grant Liens outside this covenant's reach, which is incorrect - such a Lien would still need to fit within one of the (a)-(i) exceptions.

findings.sourceEvidence: ...or assign or sell any income or revenues (including Accounts) or rights in respect of any thereof, except:
findings.proposedIrEvidence: "action": "OTHER", "posture": "PROHIBITION" (with no distinct representation of the assign/sell-revenue restriction; exceptions (a)-(i) are all framed exclusively in terms of types of Liens)
findings.verifierReasoning: Section 6.02 actually prohibits two distinct kinds of conduct: (1) creating/incurring/permitting Liens, and (2) assigning or selling income, revenues (including Accounts), or rights in respect thereof - a transfer that need not involve any Lien at all (e.g., an outright sale/assignment of receivables). The proposed IR's single rule uses a generic action of "OTHER" and its entire exception set (a)-(i) is worded strictly in terms of categories of Liens, giving no indication that a non-Lien sale/assignment of income or Accounts is independently restricted by this same section. A hypothetical transaction - a Loan Party selling its accounts receivable outright without granting any security interest - would be prohibited by the real source text (since it is not carved out by any of exceptions (a)-(i), which are Lien-specific) but the proposed IR gives no operative signal that this scenario is covered at all, creating a real risk that a reviewer relying on the IR would conclude it is unrestricted.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: "description": "Lien must constitute a 'Permitted Encumbrance' - a defined categorical list including tax liens not yet due, mechanics'/materialmen's liens not overdue >60 days, workers' comp/social security deposits, surety/appeal/performance bond deposits, certain judgment liens, easements/zoning restrictions not securing monetary obligations, commodity/brokerage margin deposits, specified contractual setoff rights, utility/governmental security deposits, and certain Canadian Priority Payables liens - excluding, in each case, any Lien securing Indebtedness except as to clauses (d) and (e) of that definition", "sufficiency": "COMPLETE"
findings.verifierReasoning: The operative source text provided says only '(b) Permitted Encumbrances;' and cross-references a defined term. The context bundle supplied to this review explicitly states 'Retrieved context items: (none)', meaning the actual text of the 'Permitted Encumbrances' definition (§1.01) was never retrieved or provided anywhere in what I was given. Yet the proposed IR asserts a highly specific, itemized enumeration of that definition's contents (down to a >60-day overdue threshold for mechanics' liens and carve-outs referencing clauses (d) and (e)) and marks this rule's sufficiency as COMPLETE. Per the verification standard, a COMPLETE claim deserves the most scrutiny, and here the specificity of the asserted content is not traceable to any evidence in the record - it cannot be verified as faithful to the real definition and may be fabricated or drawn from an unrelated/unverified source, which is exactly the kind of unsupported addition that should not be marked COMPLETE.
